- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; apply downward bias correction.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast slope or add lagged mean reversion.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 60), model overreacts; cap forecast at 5–10% above recent low.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and price is falling, model often underestimates further drop; add 2–5% downward buffer.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently fails to capture early volatility; use sentiment-weighted moving average to smooth initial forecast.
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.33, 1.00, 0.33), model may misread trend; use sentiment momentum to adjust forecast direction.
